newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean rights offering plans down 58.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean rights offering plans down 58.3 pct.

text.p: Twelve South Korean firms plan rights offerings worth 252.9 billion won for payment in August, down 58.3 percent in value from a year earlier, the Korean Listed Companies' Association said on Friday.
The subscription period would be earlier than the payment period.
The biggest offering will be made by Korea Long-Term Credit Bank, which plans to issue 10.1 million new shares for payment by August 19.
It would raise the bank's paid-in capital to 280.88 billion won from the current 230.38 billion won, the association said.
